title: A white teacher tries to swap horns
summary: A Little Rock saxophone teacher tries to trade his blue 'jazz' sax for Pillars's horn, so Pillars stops taking lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: That was because they couldn't play saxophone at all. They couldn't play saxophone, and they didn't know as much about it as I did. But what happened, there was -- I found there was a white teacher that taught saxophone and lived in Little Rock. I contacted him. I went to him and took one lesson. But what he tried to do, he tried to con me
into swapping my horn for his horn.

Now, my horn was a silver-plated with a gold bell -- with a gold plated bell instrument. He had what's called a blue jazz saxophone. It was a -- can't think of the name now -- off brand, and it was painted blue. They called it blue jazz. And he got mad at me because I wouldn't switch, and swap my horn for his horn.

So, I said, well, I don't need a guy like him to be teaching me, you know what I mean, if he was going to try to rob me out of my brand new horn -- and my horn wasn't even paid for -- quite paid for. Do you know what I mean?
